evidence.note: Class I: a string literal is evidence that a translation unit containing it was compiled in, not proof that the code around it is reachable, and its ABSENCE is evidence only when a control literal of the same kind, from the same file, is present. The literal_reads carry only offsets, lengths and bytes. What we would see if the preprocessor readings were wrong: a hit on one of the rows predicted absent while its controls are present.

probes.why: the tail of FPakPlatformFile::Mount. Present iff the legacy pak mount code was linked at all.
the sibling-.utoc branch of FPakPlatformFile::Mount, the only place a non-global container reaches FFilePackageStoreBackend.
the branch a bare .pak with no sibling .utoc takes; it sets bIoStoreSuccess = false while the pak still enters PakFiles.

probes.text: Deferring mount of pak "%s" until encryption key '%s' becomes available
probes.why: the EncryptionKeyGuid gate, the only key check inside Mount.

probes.text: assets in this pak file may not be accessible until a corresponding UFS Mount Point is added through FPackageName::RegisterMountPoint.
probes.why: the only mount-point-shaped admission remark in the pak path. It is a Display log, not a rejection; presence lets a reader check that for themselves.

probes.text: Falling back to imperfect hashmap for container '%s'
probes.why: FFileIoStoreReader::Initialize, the per-container TOC intake.
unconditional log in FFileIoStoreReader::Initialize; a control for the signature probes below, which are conditional.
FFilePackageStoreBackend::GetPackageRedirectInfo -- the package store backend that turns a container header into loadable package ids.

reachable only when IsSigningEnabled() can return true, and IsSigningEnabled (IoStore.cpp:61-68) is `return GetPakSigningKeysDelegate().IsBound()` under UE_BUILD_SHIPPING and a literal false otherwise. Declared unknown because MSVC is not obliged to drop an unreferenced literal, so a hit is weak evidence and a miss is strong.

inside #if ALT2_ENABLE_LINKERLOAD_SUPPORT, which is #defined to WITH_EDITOR at AsyncLoading2.cpp:263-264. A hit would mean this build kept the file-system fallback that lets AsyncLoading2 load a legacy .uasset with no package-store entry -- which would change the answer for a mod in a legacy pak.

probes.text: Package %s might be missing an import from cooked package %s because it's exports are not yet ready.
probes.why: second, independently placed string inside the same #if.

probes.text: Script object %s (0x%016llX) is missing a NotifyRegistrationEvent from the initial load phase.
probes.why: reached through `#elif DO_CHECK` in FGlobalImportStore::RegistrationComplete (4953-4966). DO_CHECK is 0 in a Shipping build, so a hit says this image is not Shipping -- a discriminator for D-04, measured here as a by-product rather than assumed.
inside #if !UE_BUILD_SHIPPING in FPakPlatformFile::GetPakFolders. If absent, the only pak directories this build ever scans are the three hardcoded ones, which bounds mod discovery.
inside #if !UE_BUILD_SHIPPING in MountAllPakFiles.
inside #if !UE_BUILD_SHIPPING in FPakPlatformFile::Initialize.
the three hardcoded pak folders are built with FString::Printf(TEXT("%sPaks/"), ...); the literal survives in any configuration.

the native-class registration step the source chain ends on. A Verbose UE_LOG, so its survival depends on the build's logging configuration and not on the code path being present; declared unknown so that neither outcome can be read as evidence about the path.

probes.text: Could not find class object for %s
probes.why: inside FAsyncPackage2::EventDrivenCreateExport, the place where an export -- a UClass export included -- becomes a UObject on the IoStore path.

the operand of PakFilename.EndsWith inside FPakPlatformFile::Mount itself. Its presence is evidence that Mount was compiled into this image; it also names the ONLY filename-derived rule inside Mount, and that rule adjusts PakOrder, i.e. precedence, and nothing else.
FPaths::ChangeExtension(InPakFilename, TEXT(".utoc")) inside Mount -- the sibling-container rule that decides whether a mounted pak contributes package-store entries at all.
the Printf format in FPakPlatformFile::Initialize whose FileExists result gates creation of the IoStore file backend and of FFilePackageStoreBackend.
FFileIoStoreReader::Initialize builds the payload path from it.
the partition suffix in the same function; a second, independently placed literal from that translation unit.
ALL_PAKS_WILDCARD -- the pattern FindAllPakFiles matches, so the shape of automatic discovery: any *.pak in the scanned folders, with no name allowlist.

an FParse::Param literal in this file that is NOT inside #if !UE_BUILD_SHIPPING. Control for the three switches predicted absent: if this one is present and those are absent, the absences are the preprocessor and not a general stripping of FParse literals.
second such control, in FindPakFilesInDirectory.
third such control; also the switch that turns on CheckIoStoreContainerBlockSignatures at mount time.
inside #if !UE_BUILD_SHIPPING in FPakPlatformFile::Initialize; fourth member of the shipping-gate group.
a switch arm of LexToString(EAsyncPackageLoadingState2), compiled in every configuration. THE control for the two ALT2 arms below: same function, adjacent lines.

an arm of the SAME switch, inside #if ALT2_ENABLE_LINKERLOAD_SUPPORT. Present-vs-absent against the control above is a controlled test of that macro in this image, and the macro decides whether AsyncLoading2 can load a package that has no package-store entry.
a second arm inside the same #if.
a second unconditional arm, after the #if, so the control is not a single point.
FIoStoreTocHeader::TocMagicImg. A char[] and therefore ASCII, not UTF-16LE; it is the byte string CheckMagic compares against and it is present in every container this install ships.

probes.source: not engine source: the packaged-game bootstrap's own target
probes.why: expected present only in the small root-level launcher, absent in the two game binaries. Its presence there is what makes MISERY-Win64-Shipping.exe 'the shipped image' for this question.

probes.source: not engine source: the bootstrap's own module name
probes.why: identifies the launcher as UE's BootstrapPackagedGame.
argument of an IsTimeLimitExceeded call inside the ALT2 #if.
second such argument inside the ALT2 #if.
third such argument inside the ALT2 #if.
the matching control: same kind of call, same file, OUTSIDE the #if. If the controls are absent too, the test is void rather than negative, and must be reported that way.
second control, in the function that resolves a package request.
third control.

the package-name literal UObjectBase::Register compares against for per-module bootstrap. Native class registration takes its package name from literals like this one, in the image, and never from a container.
